records.description: This is a green glass ennol.  The body is made from green glass.  The strings are made from giant cave spider silk.  The bow is made from copper.    The ennol is a large hand-held silk-stringed instrument with a glass body.  The instrument rests flat as the musician plays the forty strings with a metal bow.  Tuning is possible with adjustable bridges.  The instrument has a four-and-a-half octave range going from a low to a high pitch.  It has four registers.  The low register has a sparse floating timbre.  The middle register begins at mid-low pitch and has a delicate quavering strident timbre.  The high register begins at middle pitch and has a quavering harsh nasal buzzy timbre.  The top register begins at mid-high pitch and has a full quavering harsh timbre.

records.description: This is a well-crafted wolverine bone adesh.    The adesh is a large hand-held wind instrument consisting of thirteen adjacent cylindrical bone pipes.  The musician blows through a double reed in each pipe.  The instrument has a three octave range going from a very low to a middle pitch.  At all pitches, the instrument has a evolving wobbling timbre.  It has two registers.  The low register has a quavering watery timbre.  The high register begins at low pitch and has a raspy muddy timbre.

Tuning is possible with adjustable bridges.  The instrument has a four-and-a-half octave range going from a low to a high pitch.  It has four registers.  The low register has a sparse floating timbre.  The middle register begins at mid-low pitch and has a delicate quavering strident timbre.  The high register begins at middle pitch and has a quavering harsh nasal buzzy timbre.  The top register begins at mid-high pitch and has a full quavering harsh timbre.

rows: [C:7:0:1]The Valley of Winds is a light poetic form intended to teach a moral lesson concerning the hunt, originating in The Big Channel.  The rules of the form are applied by poets to produce individual poems which can be recited.  The poem is four sexains.  Use of consonance and metaphor is characteristic of the form.  A form of parallelism is common throughout the poem, in that certain lines reverse grammatical structures.  Each line has three syllables.  The rhyme scheme of the poem is AAAABA.

[C:7:0:1]The Intricate Luxuries is a form of music used for entertainment originating in The Big Channel.  The form guides musicians during improvised performances.  The music is played on a ekast and a shùrrat.  The musical voices bring melody and counterpoint.  The melody has long phrases, while the counterpoint has phrases of varied length throughout the form.  The music repeats for as long as necessary.  It is performed using the berim scale.  [B]The ekast always should be spirited.  [B]The shùrrat always does the main melody and should stress the rhythm.  [B]The Intricate Luxuries has a well-defined multi-passage structure: a lengthy introduction, a verse and a chorus all repeated two times and a coda.  [B]The introduction is voiced by the melody of the shùrrat and the counterpoint of the ekast.  The passage is at a hurried pace, and it is to be in whispered undertones.  This passage typically has some sparse chords.  The passage is performed in the sákrith rhythm.  [B]The verse is voiced by the melody of the shùrrat.  The passage is extremely fast, and it is to be moderately soft.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage.  The passage is performed in free rhythm.  [B]The chorus is voiced by the melody of the ekast and the melody of the shùrrat.  The passage is half the tempo of the last passage, and it is to become softer and softer.  This passage features only melodic tones and intervals.  The passage is performed in free rhythm.  [B]The coda is voiced by the melody of the shùrrat.  The passage is slow, and it is to fade into silence.  Only one pitch is ever played at a time in this passage.  The passage is performed in free rhythm.  [B]Scales are conceived of as two chords built using a division of the perfect fourth interval into eight notes.  The tonic note is fixed only at the time of performance.  [B]As always, the berim pentatonic scale is thought of as two disjoint chords drawn from the fundamental division of the perfect fourth.  These chords are named bidok and mabdug.  [B]The bidok trichord is the 1st, the 2nd and the 8th degrees of the fundamental perfect fourth division.  [B]The mabdug trichord is the 1st, the 5th and the 8th degrees of the fundamental perfect fourth division.  [B]The sákrith rhythm is made from two patterns: the agêk (considered the primary) and the lanlar.  The patterns are to be played over the same period of time, concluding together regardless of beat number.  [B]The agêk rhythm is a single line with thirty-two beats divided into four bars in a 8-8-8-8 pattern.  The beats are named ucat (spoken uc), ngárak (ngá), enir (en), ugath (ug), lisig (li), etäg (et), erong (er) and osed (os).  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| - - - - - - x - | x ! x x x x x x | - x - - x - - - | X x - x x x - x | [B]where ! marks the primary accent, X marks an accented beat, x is a beat, - is silent and | indicates a bar.  [B]The lanlar rhythm is a single line with two beats.  The beats are named udir (spoken ud) and tarmid (ta).  The beat is stressed as follows:[B]| x x | [B]where x is a beat and | indicates a bar.

[C:7:0:1]The Wispy Berry is a performance partner dance originating in The Big Channel.  The rules of the form are applied by choreographers to produce individual dances which can be performed.  The dance is accompanied by The Intricate Luxuries.  The dancers perform in a single line turning counterclockwise.  This dance is a refined artform, with one special position to be mastered.  The dance is punctuated by vivacious independent body movement.  [B]The dance begins with the introduction of the music.  The dancers perform quickly to the sákrith rhythm.  The partners dance closely, communicating intent by pulling away.  This section is punctuated by the sensual spins of the lead.  [B]The dance enters a new section with the verse of the music.  The dancers perform very quickly with the music.  The partners rarely make contact, communicating intent through visual cues.  This crude flamboyant section is punctuated by the forward bends of the lead, kicks and energetic counterclockwise eighth turns.  [B]The dance enters a new section with the chorus of the music.  The dancers perform slowly with the music.  The partners dance closely, communicating intent by pushing together.  This intense section is punctuated by softly percussive footwork.  [B]The dance enters a new section with the coda of the music.  The dancers perform slowly with the music.  The partners dance closely, communicating intent by pushing together.  This section is punctuated by vivacious leaps and serene counterclockwise eighth turns.  [B]The âtrid the fundamental dance position.  There should be a passive hand gesture from the follower with a grotesque leg lift.
